plain_english: The supplied page is Andrew Glasgow's testament-testamentar and inventory. His residence is provisionally read as Corsoun in the parish of Caldercleir, sheriffdom of Edinburgh. It records his death on 7 February and says that he gave up the inventory himself on 6 February. The latter-will opening at the bottom expressly bears 6 February 1597 as written.

The inventory includes cows with calves, young cattle, horses, sheep, oats, barley, household furnishings and clothing. Incoming and outgoing accounts name financial associates, but their appearance here does not establish family relationships.

Selected family clauses on image 124 were freshly inspected on 27 September 2026. They explicitly name Robert as Andrew’s son by his wife Elizat, provide conditionally for a possible pregnancy, and name Marion, Jonet and Isobel in the children’s distribution provision. The cancelled daughter word remains marked. These excerpts prove the named children’s relationship to Andrew; they do not identify the girls’ mother or establish Jonet’s possible later identity as the 1624 Mid Calder Ramsy bride.
findings: Image 123, lines 4-9: this is a testament-testamentar, distinct from a testament-dative. The decedent's own act on the sixth and death on the seventh are legible; uncertain year numerals in the opening should be checked against the clearer 1597 at the latter-will opening.

Image 123, line 42: 6 February 1597 is the written latter-will date. The existing record describes this as 1597/8 under the pre-1600 Scottish year convention; that is a dating interpretation, not a different date written on the image.
Image 123, lines 24-36: financial associates and possible Stevenson names are not described here as Andrew's parents, children or siblings.

Image 124: selected family clauses freshly reviewed. Jonet is named with Marion and Isobel in the testament’s child-distribution provision. Glasgow-3183 now represents the testament-defined daughter after the Glasgow-4096 merger, so Andrew’s father status was upgraded to confident and verified live on 27 September. The later marriage attribution remains probable. The page has not received a full diplomatic transcription.
changes_from_previous: Earlier 10 September review retained partial coverage: image 123 was transcribed, while image 124 still awaited fresh reading. The selected family clauses have now been reviewed; the remaining continuation still needs full transcription.
Freshly supports the testament type, Caldercleir setting, sixth/seventh-February sequence and the written 1597 latter-will date.

At the 10 September review, Elizat Stevinsoun, Robert and the named daughters were findings of the older continuation review. The selected clauses have now been freshly inspected on 27 September, without attempting a complete page-two transcription.
The outgoing Stevenson name may be patrik rather than James in one entry. The present reading is too uncertain for an identity correction; retain a flagged financial-name query.

27 September 2026: supersedes the earlier awaiting-review status for selected image-124 family clauses. Records fresh inspection and selected excerpts, while retaining partial coverage and the cancelled word. Andrew–Jonet parentage is direct; the later Ramsy identity remains separately probable.

confidence_statement: Fresh visual review of image 123 and enlarged crops in the earlier attempt, supplemented by fresh inspection of selected image-124 family clauses on 27 September 2026. High confidence in the document type, written latter-will date, Robert’s explicit parentage and named children in the distribution provision; moderate confidence in locality; low confidence in many financial names and sums. Coverage remains partial: the continuation excerpts are non-contiguous and do not reconstruct intervening text. Later identity attribution to the 1624 Ramsy bride remains probable.
